title: Reading a midnight signal
bodyMd:
A town installed flow meters at the entrances to three water districts. One district continued to receive substantial water between two and four in the morning, when household demand was expected to be low. Engineers considered hidden leakage a possible explanation, but they did not immediately estimate the lost water by treating every overnight litre as a leak. The district also contained a bakery operating before dawn and a hospital with continuous demand.

The engineers first obtained consumption records from these large users and compared several nights rather than relying on one reading. They then used temporary meters to narrow the area in which unexplained flow persisted. The procedure did not assume that unusual demand was harmless; it separated legitimate consumption from the residual flow that required investigation.
